text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Stability pact agreement smooths path towards European Monetary Union
- Opposition leader Lafontaine says child benefit will not be cut as part of austerity measures
- Foreign Minister Kinkel restates German claim to permanent seat on United Nations Security Council
- DIHT Federation of Chambers of Commerce restates demand for slimmed-down government and administration
- Retail workers in key state of North Rhine-Westphalia agree pay settlement which maintains full sick pay
- New agriculture bill to be revised again before going to parliament
HANDELSBLATT
- EU finance ministers agree new exchange rate mechanism
- Economics Minister Rexrodt sees electricity and gas monopolies being opened up in first half of 1997
- Machine tool prices under pressure, sector expected to stagnate in 1996
- CDU/CSU medium-sized business association under investigation
- Controversy deepens over implementation of cut in statutory sick pay
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- EMU stability pact agreed
- Stuttgart mayor Rommel wants to see more foreigners naturalised in Germany
- RWI economic institute president Heilemann says unemployment will only decline if economic growth reaches two percent
- Study shows few firms are ready for electronic marketplace
- Bavarian state premier Stoiber adds to calls for better deal for German farmers from EU
DIE WELT
- EU stability pact to guarantee strength of new European currency
- Opposition Social Democrats in favour of German participation in new Balkan peacekeeping force
- Brussels bureaucrats accused of having been careless in investigation of mad cow disease
- Government wants to cut coal subsidy earlier than planned
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 2609760
